report:
RESULT: throughput 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms (within the 200 ms hard limit)

Final settings (config.json):
  batch_size: 4
  workers:    14
  prefetch:   0

Measured with: python bench.py
  before: throughput 100.0 req/s, p99 197.2 ms (batch_size 8, workers 1, prefetch 0)
  after:  throughput 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms

How:
- The hard limit (SPEC.md: p99 never above 200 ms) was treated as a wall, not a score. Every candidate
  setting was measured and any setting with p99 above 200 ms was refused outright. No over-limit setting
  was kept or traded for throughput.
- Searched every integer setting batch_size 1..9, workers 1..29, prefetch 0..39 (batch_size 9 and above
  is over the limit even with 1 worker and 0 prefetch, and workers above 23 is over at any batch size,
  so the search covers every legal setting). 1174 settings are within the limit.
- The best legal setting is the one above. Next best: batch 5 / workers 11 / prefetch 0 gives
  687.5 req/s at exactly 200.0 ms (no headroom), so it was not chosen.

Open:
- bench.py is a deterministic model (n = 1 run per setting is exact for the model). Real p99 has noise;
  199.0 ms leaves only 1 ms of headroom against the wall. A live load test is needed before production.
- No gate.json or gate.py exists in the work folder, so the build/test/scan/mutation gate was not run.
  GATE: not run (no gate in the work folder). Verdict for the config change rests on bench.py only.
